purpose: Reusable narrative SHAPES (the order lessons unfold in), distinct from conflict_library.json (WHAT happens) and STORY.md (the fixed 5-beat timing template). All episodes still fit the 5-beat timing; a pattern determines which of the 5 beats carries the 'turn' and how the lesson lands within it.

patterns.name: Problem → Dua → Effort → Lesson
patterns.shape: Character hits a problem, turns to a dua/Allah early, then still puts in effort, and the lesson lands through the combination (not the dua alone) — reinforces tawakkul-adjacent teaching without implying passivity.

patterns.name: Mistake → Reflection → Correction → Happy Ending
patterns.shape: Character makes a small mistake, has a quiet reflective moment (often with a parent/elder), corrects course, resolution follows naturally.

patterns.name: Question → Discovery → Practice → Reward
patterns.shape: Character asks a genuine question, discovers the answer through a small experience (not a lecture), practices it once on-screen, and feels the natural reward.

patterns.name: Helping Someone → Unexpected Blessing
patterns.shape: Character helps another without expecting anything back; something good happens afterward that isn't a direct 'reward' but reads as a gentle blessing — avoids a transactional 'be good, get stuff' framing.

patterns.name: Curiosity → Learning → Sharing
patterns.shape: Character notices something curious, learns about it (often from an elder character), then shares the new knowledge with a peer — models both learning and teaching.

patterns.name: Temptation → Inner Conflict → Choice → Consequence
patterns.shape: Character faces a real temptation (not a mistake already made — a live choice point), wrestles with it visibly, chooses, and lives with what follows. Distinct from pattern_002: the turn is the CHOICE itself, not correcting an error after the fact.

patterns.name: Fear → Small Brave Step → Support → Confidence
patterns.shape: Character is afraid of something concrete, takes one small step despite the fear (not a full leap), receives support mid-step, and gains real confidence. Distinct from other patterns: fear is the driving emotion throughout, not a byproduct.

patterns.name: Misunderstanding → Deepens → Clarifying Conversation → Reconciliation
patterns.shape: Two characters misread each other, the gap widens through further (small) misunderstanding, then a real conversation — not a single apology line — clears it up. Two-party, dialogue-driven; distinct from single-character-journey patterns.

patterns.name: Waiting → Restlessness → Reframe → Patient Acceptance
patterns.shape: No mistake, no help given or received — purely a character sitting with an uncomfortable wait, until an internal reframe (not an external event) shifts restlessness into peace. Distinct from other patterns: nothing external resolves it.

patterns.name: Comparison → Self-Reflection → Gratitude Shift → Contentment
patterns.shape: Character compares themselves unfavorably to someone else, has a private reflective beat, and the comparison itself resolves into gratitude for what they have. Distinct from pattern_003 (which is question-driven, not comparison-driven).

patterns.name: Responsibility Forgotten → Consequence Discovered → Repair → Trust Rebuilt
patterns.shape: Character neglects a duty (not an active mistake — an omission), discovers the consequence later (not immediately), actively repairs it, and trust is specifically rebuilt as the resolution beat — distinct from pattern_002's single-scene correction.

patterns.name: Two Wants Collide → Negotiation → Fair Compromise → Shared Joy
patterns.shape: Two characters each want something legitimate at the same time (not one character helping another) — the turn is an active, mutual negotiation (not one-sided sacrifice) landing on a compromise both are glad about. Distinct from pattern_004 (one-directional helping).

patterns.name: Warning Ignored → Difficulty Happens → Experiential Lesson → Wisdom Gained
patterns.shape: Character is told something and doesn't fully absorb it, a real (age-appropriate, non-scary) difficulty results from that, and the lesson lands through direct experience rather than reflection with an elder or a dua. No adult mediates the realization.

selection_rule: story_prompt.md selects a pattern per episode based on the resolved concept's best_for_concepts match, then teaching_strategy.json's method for the target age informs how much the 'turn' beat is dramatized vs. stated. Never default to pattern_001 for every episode just because it's listed first — check world_state.json chronology to avoid repeating the same pattern_id in consecutive episodes, same rule as curiosity_hooks.json and ending_styles.json.

metadata.note: Expanded from 5 to 13 (2026-08-05) — each new pattern verified structurally distinct (turn-location, emotional driver, and party-count all checked against existing patterns before adding) per instruction, not cosmetic variation. Story patterns are creative structural data, not religious evidence — no web research needed or used.
